prompt: Quitanda moves its orders database to Azure SQL Database. Which of these is still Quitanda's job?
hint: The left column of the table is Microsoft's.

choices.text: Applying the engine's patches
choices.why: The service applies them, in a window you can influence.

choices.text: Adding the index a slow report needs
choices.why: Right: the engine runs your queries as you wrote them.

choices.text: Taking a backup every night and testing the restore
choices.why: Backups and point-in-time restore are the service's.

choices.text: Replacing a disk that failed
choices.why: The hardware is Microsoft's.

prompt: What is an Azure SQL logical server?
hint: You never log into it.

choices.text: The virtual machine its databases run on
choices.why: Its databases may each run on different hardware.

choices.text: A SQL Server instance with its own SQL Agent
choices.why: There is no instance, and no SQL Agent.

choices.text: A name and settings: the login, firewall rules and auditing
choices.why: Right, and the databases under it are bought one by one.

choices.text: The unit Azure bills compute by
choices.why: Compute is billed per database, or per pool.

prompt: What is the longest point-in-time retention, in days, that `retention_days` accepts for an Azure SQL database?
hint: The provider's message printed the range.

prompt: What does a point-in-time restore of the orders database produce?
hint: The old one is not touched.

choices.text: The same database, rewound in place
choices.why: A restore never overwrites; it creates.

choices.text: A new database beside the old one
choices.why: Right: you compare, then switch or copy.

choices.text: A file of the last nightly backup, to download
choices.why: Any second in the retention period, and into a database.

choices.text: A copy in the paired region, for disaster recovery
choices.why: That is geo-restore or replication, not this.

choices.text: NULL

choices.text: It is only filled in after the first automatic backup has run

prompt: Before the index, `STATISTICS IO` reported 337 logical reads. What does one logical read count?

choices.text: A row the query returned

choices.text: An 8 KB page touched
choices.why: Right, whether it came from memory or disk.

choices.text: A request the client sent to the server
choices.why: It was one request.

choices.text: A DTU spent on the query
choices.why: DTUs are a rate of the service, not a count of pages.

prompt: On Azure, the support query runs without the index on `GP_Gen5_2`. What does moving to `GP_Gen5_8` do for it?

choices.text: Turns the scan into a seek, since a bigger tier has more indexes

choices.text: The scan gets quicker and still reads 337 pages, now at four times the price
choices.why: Right: the size hides the missing index and bills for hiding it.

choices.text: Nothing, since compute has no effect on reads
choices.why: More vCores and memory make the same reads finish sooner.

choices.text: It reads only the pages that changed since the last query
choices.why: A scan reads the table, whatever changed.

choices.text: Both models, in the same way

choices.text: vCore, through the Azure Hybrid Benefit

prompt: At an illustrative 0.25 USD per vCore-hour and a month of 730 hours, what does a provisioned `GP_Gen5_4` cost in compute for a month, in USD?
hint: The last part of the name is the vCores.

prompt: In the SKU name `GP_S_Gen5_2`, the letter ___ says the database is serverless.
hint: Between the tier and the hardware.

prompt: What is a paused serverless database billed for?
hint: The data is still there.

choices.text: Its minimum vCores
choices.why: The minimum is the floor while it runs, not while paused.

choices.text: Its storage, and no compute
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: Nothing at all until it resumes
choices.why: Storage is billed every hour, paused or not.

choices.text: Its maximum vCores, held ready for the resume
choices.why: Nothing is held; the compute is released.

prompt: At the illustrative 0.36 USD per vCore-hour of `breakeven.py`, what does one day cost for a serverless database busy 4 hours at 2 vCores, then online 1 hour at its 0.5 minimum before pausing, in USD?
hint: Add the vCore-hours, then multiply.

prompt: Quitanda's orders database takes orders from seven in the morning to midnight, every day. Why is provisioned compute the right purchase?
hint: Two reasons, one from the table and one from the resume.

choices.text: Serverless is not offered in General Purpose
choices.why: It is: `GP_S_Gen5_2`.

choices.text: Busy past the break-even, and a pause would fail a customer
choices.why: Right: 17 busy hours costs more serverless, and a resume delays the first order.

choices.text: Provisioned is always cheaper than serverless, at any number of hours
choices.why: Below about 16 hours a day serverless was cheaper.

choices.text: A serverless database cannot hold more than 32 GB
choices.why: That was the development copy's own `max_size_gb`.

prompt: When does an elastic pool lose to sizing each database on its own?

choices.text: When the databases are bought in the vCore model

choices.text: It works, and each database takes up to 500 eDTUs

choices.text: Azure accepts it and bills the pool as 500 eDTUs
